A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSQL research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning simulations on chain and grid-world environments in Appendix A and Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation results on both environments, including cumulative-regret curves and variability across runs.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes the central target-action rule from maximizing the posterior mean to maximizing mean plus standard deviation. Equation 10 also adds a log(1/δ) factor to the Gaussian scale specification. These change the procedure, although v2 inconsistently describes the target elsewhere using a variance offset and an all-action maximum.

E1.justification: Appendix A retains the same stochastic chain and 4×4 grid-world environments, with identical task requirements and environment-generation rules. No evaluated domain or scenario is added.

E2.justification: Figures 1–2 retain UCBQL, RLSVI, and Staged-RandQL as comparators for PSQL*. Figure 3 retains the comparison among PSQL*, PSQL, and UCBQL.

E3.justification: Appendix A is unchanged, including horizon H=32, cumulative-regret evaluation, initialization, and tuned experimental constants. The revised theoretical algorithm specification does not establish a change to the reported experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The single-sample versus modified-target comparison in Figure 3 is retained unchanged. Neither version adds further ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or error analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 10 randomly generated environment instances and error bars representing one standard deviation. No empirical run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All five plot images comprising Figures 1–3 are identical across versions. Appendix A also retains the same performance findings, with no empirical result entries added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Appendices C–E substantially revise the optimism, action-mismatch, and concentration arguments. v2 adds Proposition 2, an expectation assumption to Lemma 2, and a Bernstein martingale lemma; it replaces v1 Lemma 12’s iterative concentration argument with v2 Lemma 11 and a different bound. Lemma 5’s probability changes to Φ(-2)-Aδ. The leading regret rates and existing Appendix F extension remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: Gaussian-posterior Q-learning, the regularized-ELBO interpretation, promising empirical performance, and a regret rate of order H²√SAT up to logarithmic factors.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 revises the error-accumulation explanation to emphasize multiple samples used for decision-making as well as target construction, and explains the target-action uncertainty offset. The empirical interpretations and stated future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Equation 11 revises the implementable prescription for J(δ), replacing the denominator log(1/(1-p1)) with log(4/(4-p1)) and replacing δ′ with δ in p1. Appendix A’s practical implementation and tuning disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cesa-Bianchi and Lugosi’s Prediction, Learning, and Games to support the new martingale concentration lemma. The remaining references and positioning relative to prior reinforcement-learning methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4.1 receive localized explanatory rewrites, and Appendix C reorders action-mismatch, target-error, and optimism arguments. Most introductory prose, the conclusion, and the overall document organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1’s caption now identifies PSQL* as a heuristic derived from PSQL. Algorithm 2 gains an explanatory comment, and revised proofs cause local reflow. The empirical plots and Table 1 retain their displays.

improvement.justification: v2 makes sample independence explicit and adds reasoning connecting target selection to optimism. However, Algorithm 2’s mean-plus-standard-deviation rule conflicts with Section 3.2’s variance-offset and all-action formulas, while Appendix A still describes the old mean-only rule. Lemma 2’s proof also invokes the opposite inequality from its newly stated expectation assumption. These unresolved conflicts affect the central method, proof, and connection to the retained experiments, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
